title: [D0 Foundations] Version registry for every recorded version dimension
summary: `helena.versions` now exists: `VersionSet` is a frozen Pydantic model of the eight dimensions concept/07-principles.md names (model, prompt, schema, rendering, taxonomy, enrichment snapshot, policy, aggregation), every one required with no default, whose field names are the column names — `stamp(row)` adds them and refuses a row that already carries one, `from_row(row)` is the replay direction and names any dimension the row does not record. The aggregation version exists twice, as `AGGREGATION_VERSION` and as the view `helena_aggregation_version` created by `sql/migrations/0002_aggregation_version.sql`, and a test asserts the two equal by applying the migrations to a throwaway engine and selecting from the view rather than by reading the file. The 'a revision is a new version module, never an edit' rule is written down in docs/decisions/0008-version-registry.md, the README and the runbook, with the bump procedure.
assumption_validated: Two results, one positive and one negative. POSITIVE: a version constant can live in SQL and in Python with the drift caught by execution — the equality test was mutation-checked (changing only the Python constant fails it), so the duplication the concept requires is actually policed rather than merely declared. NEGATIVE, and the more useful one: the assumption that the SQL copy could be the single place a downstream view reads the version from is FALSE on RisingWave 3.0.3. A streaming query cannot reference the one-row constant view at all — `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... CROSS JOIN helena_aggregation_version`, the same thing as `JOIN ... ON true`, and the same thing as a scalar subquery are each rejected with 'Not supported: streaming nested-loop join', while a batch SELECT over the view is fine. So a D2 aggregation view must carry the literal itself and assert its own equality against `AGGREGATION_VERSION` on the rows it produces. That limitation is pinned by a test so a later engine version lifting it becomes news rather than folklore.
makes_buildable: Anything that writes a citable row can stamp it: `VersionSet(...).stamp(row)` returns the row with the eight version columns, `VERSION_COLUMNS` names them for the migration that first declares them, and `VersionSet.from_row(row)` is what replay validates against. The D2 context/aggregation tasks have the aggregation version to stamp, the measured rule for how to stamp it (a literal in the view, plus a test on the produced rows), and a runbook procedure for bumping it. The D3 taxonomy task has the 'new version module beside the old one, never an edit' rule written down before there is a taxonomy to edit. The D4/D5 agent and assessment tasks have a version set that refuses to be completed from current constants, and `helena.observability`'s `versions=` argument now has a concrete producer (`VersionSet.as_columns()`), demonstrated by a test.

verification.command: make check  (uv lock --check; compileall; uv run pytest -q)
verification.detail: 176 passed in 13.7 s from cold with no infrastructure running — the conftest fixture started an in-memory RisingWave itself. 20 of those are new: 17 unit and 3 that execute migration 0002 against a throwaway engine (the SQL/Python equality, that the engine really reports the object as a VIEW, and that a streaming view is refused when it tries to read it). The equality test was mutation-checked: setting AGGREGATION_VERSION to 'v2' with the SQL unchanged fails it with 'At index 0 diff: (v1,) != (v2,)'. The by-hand deployment path was also run against a real engine: `uv run scripts/migrate.py --status` listed both files pending, `uv run scripts/migrate.py` applied both, and `SELECT aggregation_version FROM helena_aggregation_version` in `public` returned 'v1' with the catalog reporting table_type 'VIEW'. No credential was read, printed or stored; the only .env access was through helena.config for the engine DSN.

deferred: The 'column default' half of PRD step 2 was deliberately not taken; the SQL copy is a constant view instead. Two reasons, both recorded in docs/decisions/0008: there is no assessment table yet and inventing one here would be writing the D3/D4 contract ahead of the increment that needs it (a contract field is an escalation), and a column DEFAULT is a silent fallback for a writer that forgot to record a version — the one thing a version registry may not do. The step offered 'SQL constant/column default', so this is a choice within it, not a departure from it.

No values for the seven dimensions that do not exist yet. Prompts, renderings, taxonomy modules, feed snapshots and policies arrive in D2-D5; a constant invented now would be a version for nothing. `model_version` is documented as the identity the model's response reported, not the configured name, and the increment that first calls a model owns getting it.

No version columns in SQL and no version-set identifier. Whether an assessment carries the eight columns inline or cites a version-set row is a question for the increment that writes the first assessment; deciding it now would be a join table with no rows. `VERSION_COLUMNS` is the names that migration will declare.
No ordering or comparison of version identifiers. Nothing compares two versions yet, and the token is deliberately permissive because a model version is whatever the endpoint calls itself.
No taxonomy or schema version module was created — the taxonomy is D3 and editing it is an escalation. Only the rule was written down.
lessons: task 05: RisingWave 3.0.3 cannot read a one-row constant view from a STREAMING query. `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW m AS SELECT t.x, v.c FROM t CROSS JOIN const_view v` fails with 'Not supported: streaming nested-loop join', and so do `JOIN const_view ON true` and `(SELECT c FROM const_view)` as a scalar subquery. A batch SELECT over the same view is fine. Consequence for D2: an aggregation view stamps the version as a literal in its own definition, and the test asserts the produced rows equal helena.versions.AGGREGATION_VERSION. tests/test_versions.py pins the limitation.

task 05: `information_schema.columns.column_default` is NULL in RisingWave 3.0.3 even for a column that really has a DEFAULT and really applies it — `CREATE TABLE d (x INT PRIMARY KEY, agg VARCHAR NOT NULL DEFAULT 'v1'); INSERT INTO d (x) VALUES (7)` stores ('7','v1'), and `SHOW CREATE TABLE d` shows the default text, but the information_schema column is empty. So a column default cannot be checked from information_schema; insert a row and read it back, or read SHOW CREATE TABLE.

task 05: A Pydantic field named `model_version` (or anything starting with `model_`) emits a UserWarning about the protected `model_` namespace, and pytest is configured with filterwarnings = ["error"], so it is a test failure. `ConfigDict(protected_namespaces=())` is the fix and nothing here shadows a BaseModel method.

task 05: `Redactor([])` raises by design — a redactor with nothing registered would silently redact nothing. A test that needs a StructuredLogger must register a value; a fake one is enough when the test is not about redaction.

task 05: Mutation-check an equality test between two copies of a constant before believing it. Flipping AGGREGATION_VERSION alone and watching the engine test fail is what distinguishes a real assertion from one that compares a value with itself.

task 05: A plain `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 'x' AS c` works in RisingWave, shows up in `information_schema.tables` with table_type 'VIEW', and its text is in `rw_catalog.rw_views.definition`. Selecting from it is the way to assert the constant; the catalog text is not needed and would be the 'assert on SQL text' mistake.
failed_approaches: task 05: Making the SQL copy of the aggregation version the single place a downstream view reads it from. All three formulations were tried against the engine and all three are rejected on RisingWave 3.0.3 with 'Not supported: streaming nested-loop join': CROSS JOIN against the constant view, JOIN ... ON true, and a scalar subquery in the select list. Do not retry this when writing the D2 aggregation views — carry the literal and test the produced rows.

task 05: Holding the aggregation version in a one-row TABLE was considered and rejected before it was written. An UPDATE to it would rewrite the version under rows that already recorded one, and in a streaming join it would recompute downstream rows — which is exactly the forbidden 'migrate old rows forward'. A view has no writer, and changing it needs a new migration that drops and recreates it.

task 05: Giving `VersionSet` a `current()` constructor that fills the aggregation version from the constant was considered and rejected: writing a row records what produced it and replay must take what is stored, and a set completed from current constants would be indistinguishable from one that was really recorded.
next_session_should_know: Stamp versions through `helena.versions` and nothing else. `VersionSet` requires all eight dimensions — model_version, prompt_version, schema_version, rendering_version, taxonomy_version, enrichment_snapshot_version, policy_version, aggregation_version — with no defaults, is frozen, forbids extras, hides the rejected input in validation errors (task 01's leak), and its field names ARE the column names: `versions.stamp(row)` returns a new dict with the eight columns added and refuses a row already carrying any of them, `VersionSet.from_row(row)` reads them back for replay and names what is missing, `as_columns()` is what goes into `log.info(..., versions=...)`. `VERSION_COLUMNS` is the tuple to declare in the migration that creates the first version-carrying table. Three things that will bite otherwise. (1) The aggregation version is in two places on purpose — `helena.versions.AGGREGATION_VERSION` and `sql/migrations/0002_aggregation_version.sql` — and tests/test_versions.py fails if they drift; bumping it is a NEW migration that drops and recreates the view (the runner's checksum refuses an edit to 0002), plus every aggregation view carrying the literal, in one change. docs/runbook.md §5 has the four-step procedure. (2) A streaming view CANNOT read that constant view — measured, three ways, all rejected as a nested-loop join — so a D2 aggregation view carries `'v1' AS aggregation_version` itself and needs its own test asserting the rows it produces equal AGGREGATION_VERSION. That per-view test is how the concept's 'asserted equal' invariant keeps holding once the literal spreads. (3) A revision is a new version module, never an edit: the taxonomy version and the agent schema versions get `v2` beside `v1` with `v1` left importable exactly as it was, and editing the taxonomy at all is an escalation. docs/decisions/0008-version-registry.md is the record. `helena.versions` was added to SUPPORT_MODULES in tests/test_package_layout.py — it is cross-cutting, not an eighth architecture component. Still open and untouched by this task: the concept/05 vs data/netify tension, bin/README.md's dangling reference to scripts/build-binaries.sh, and there is still no git repository, so nothing here was committed.
